Letter Sound Safari.story: Ravi went to the zoo with his teacher. At the first enclosure he heard a long 'a' sound from a lion. Next, a butterfly showed him the word 'apple'. At the bird house a hen clucked and Ravi heard the short 'u' sound in 'sun'. Last, a monkey made him laugh with the sound in 'moon'.

Listen & Do Adventure.story: Attention Class I! Please listen carefully. First, open your book to page five. Next, draw a small blue star next to the heading. Then read the three sentences aloud. After that, circle the picture of a red bus. Last, close your book and wait for the bell.

Noun Basket Sort.story: Mother gave Meera three baskets. In the first basket she put a ball, a doll and a kite. In the second basket she put a spoon, a cup and a plate. In the third basket she put Delhi, her puppy and a flower. 'Now put every naming word in the right basket,' she said.

Story Time Quiz.story: A tall tree stood near Nana's house. Every morning a small bird called Twee came to sing on its top branch. One day a storm broke the branch and Twee fell into the grass. Nana picked him up gently and kept him in a box near the window. The next morning Twee sang again, and this time a whole flock came to listen.

Announcement Detective.story: Good morning, children. This is your school announcement. The science exhibition will be held in the back hall on Monday the twelfth of June. Please bring your model by eight o'clock in the morning. The lunch break will be thirty minutes longer on that day. Students who bring paper models must label them with their name and class. Thank you.

Sound Detective.story: Anil closed his eyes and listened to his street. First he heard a bus hiss as it stopped near the corner. Then he heard a shopkeeper shouting 'Rupees twenty!' Next came a bicycle bell ringing twice. Finally he heard his mother calling him from the kitchen. Anil laughed and said, 'My street tells me a story every evening.'

Verb Action Sort.story: Every morning Sita does four things before the bus comes. First she folds her blanket and makes her bed. Next she brushes her teeth and washes her face. Then she drinks a glass of milk and eats one banana. Last of all she runs to the gate with her school bag. After school she writes her homework, packs her bag and waits for the bus.

Listen & Answer Challenge.story: The school fair opened at nine o'clock on Saturday. Reema and her brother reached the gate at nine fifteen, so they missed the dancing contest but saw the painting stall. Reema entered her painting of a peacock and won second prize. She received a geometry box and a chart of India. By four o'clock her painting was hung near the entrance for everyone to see.

Parts of Speech Sorter.story: The teacher wrote four words on the board: 'river', 'run', 'blue' and 'quickly'. She asked the children to name each word. Neha said 'river' names a thing, so it is a noun. Imran said 'run' shows an action, so it is a verb. Meera said 'blue' describes the river, so it is an adjective. Then the teacher smiled and said 'quickly' tells how Imran runs, so it is an adverb.

Follow the Steps Race.story: Here is how to make a paper boat. First take a rectangular sheet of paper and fold it in half the long way. Next fold the top corners down to make a triangle. Then open the paper slightly and press the sides together to form a hull. After that fold the bottom points upwards on both sides. Finally pull the two sides apart gently until the boat opens. Your boat is ready.

Listen & Type Challenge.story: Good morning everyone. Please write down these three sentences exactly as you hear them. Sentence one: The library opens at ten o'clock. Sentence two: Please return the books on Monday. Sentence three: The library is on the second floor, next to the reading room. When you finish, check every word before you hand in your answer sheet.

Podcast Pop Quiz.story: Welcome to our school podcast. Today we visit Uncle Khan's honey farm. Uncle Khan keeps forty bee boxes beside a field of mustard flowers. He says bees collect nectar from the flowers and turn it into honey. In one season Uncle Khan collects about nine hundred jars of honey. He then packs the jars in straw and sends them to shops in the nearby town.

Word Role Race.story: In the sentence 'The brave girl saved a small kitten', the words have different jobs. 'The' is an article. 'Brave' is an adjective because it describes the girl. 'Girl' is a noun because it names someone. 'Saved' is a verb because it shows an action. 'A' is an article again, 'small' is an adjective, 'kitten' is a noun, and the whole sentence tells us the girl performed an action.

Mission Control Orders.story: Attention team, this is mission control. Our mission begins at six o'clock. First, collect three empty bottles and two lids from the store room. Next, carry them to the laboratory on the first floor. Then wash each bottle and let it dry in the sun. After that, label each bottle with your team number. Finally, report to the science teacher. Do not begin without the gloves.

Story Time Quiz - Class V.story: Harriet looked after her grandfather's garden every summer. One year the mango tree gave only four fruits. Harriet did not discourage. She watered the roots twice a week, spread compost around the tree and removed the weeds. The following summer the tree gave more than two hundred fruits. Her grandfather smiled and said the hardest work was the watering, not the picking.

Pronunciation Match-Up.story: Listen to these pairs of words. In 'record' used as a noun, the stress falls on the first syllable, so it sounds like 'RE cord'. In 'record' used as a verb, the stress falls on the second syllable, so it sounds like 're CORD'. Similarly, 'present' is 'PRE sent' for a gift, but 'pre SENT' for a verb. Write down the word and say it twice, moving the stress each time.

Simon Says Challenge � Class VI.story: Simon says: touch your nose. Simon says: clap three times. Simon says: stand on your left foot. Nobody says: jump three times. Simon says: spell your name quietly. Simon says: count backwards from ten to six. Nobody says: sit down. Simon says: raise your right hand.

Sound Detective � Class VI.story: The science room was silent. Then a thin wire was stretched across a wooden box and a cup was fixed to its middle. Ravi plucked the wire and immediately the cup jumped. 'The wire is loose,' he said, so he tightened it by turning the peg one full turn. When he plucked again the cup jumped much higher. Then he added a thicker wire and the cup hardly moved at all.

Accent & Stress Spotter.story: In British English, the word 'schedule' is usually pronounced 'SHED yool', while many Indian speakers say 'SKED yool'. Both are understood. In British English 'ask' is 'ASK', but in American English it is 'ASK'. Notice that the same two-syllable word 'thirteen' changes its stress between British and Indian English. When you meet an unfamiliar word, say it aloud both ways and use the one you hear most often.

Announcement Detective � Class VII.story: Attention please. Platform number four will now be in use for the Rajdhani Express. The Rajdhani Express will depart from platform four at seven twenty-five in the evening. Coaches S seven and S eight will be attached at the rear. Passengers holding confirmed tickets should board now. The train will not wait for late passengers, so the last door will close five minutes before departure.

News Flash Listener.story: Good evening. In tonight's news, the state government has opened three new libraries in villages that had none. Each library will hold five thousand books. The government also says that the project to clean the river will begin next month, funded to the tune of four crore rupees. In sports, the district team won the final by twenty-two runs.

Follow the Steps Race � Class VIII.story: Here is the procedure for testing the pH of a sample. First label three clean test tubes A, B and C. Next pour five millilitres of distilled water into each tube. Then add one drop of universal indicator to tube A, two drops to tube B and three drops to tube C. After that swirl each tube gently and compare the colours with the chart. Finally record the matching colour and pH value for each tube in your notebook.

Listen & Repeat Lab.story: Let us practise tongue twisters. Say this one slowly, then faster: 'She sells seashells by the seashore.' Now try: 'Red leather, yellow leather.' Finally say: 'A proper copper coffee pot.' Notice that in each sentence the repeated sounds use different mouth movements. Record yourself the first time and the fifth time, then compare the two recordings.

Radio Ad Detective.story: You are listening to a radio advertisement. It says: 'Fresh coconut water straight from Kerala, delivered to your door in just two hours. Order before noon on Monday to get a free glass bottle. Dial 1800-222-333 now. The first one hundred callers each receive a twenty rupee discount.' The advertisement repeats three times before another programme begins.
